tossups.text: The Alborz Mountains lie north of the Dasht-e Kavir salt desert in this country. The ancient civilization of Elam was located in what is now this nation, which faced a separatist movement in Khuzestan Province. The Zagros Mountains run down the west side of this country, from its border with Azerbaijan to the Strait of Hormuz. The region of Balochistan is shared between this country and its neighbors to the southeast, Afghanistan and Pakistan. North of the Gulf of Oman is - for ten points - what nation that is home to the Persian Plateau?

One scholar working in this city was the first Greek to create a spherical model of the Earth and was named Crates. Revelation 2:12 refers to this place as the location where "Satan has his throne," and the first systematic excavations in it were carried out by Carl Humann. After this city was deprived of papyrus under King Eumenes, scholars supposedly invented parchment. This city lends its name to a "Baroque" style whose leader was Epigonos. Epigonos worked on a structure in this city that depicts its legendary founder Telephus. For 10 points, a frieze of the Gigantomachy was excavated and brought to Berlin from what ancient city in Aeolis and capital of the Attalid dynasty?

Emphysema and COPD primarily affect these organs, which are surrounded by the pleural membrane. These organs secrete pulmonary surfactant to decrease the surface tension of their alveoli. A disease of these organs which is marked by spasms in bronchi can be treated with an albuterol inhaler. For 10 points, name the primary organs affected by asthma, which expand and contract during breathing and provide oxygen to the body.

The Urdu film Khoon Ka Khoon was the first with sound to be made about this character, who "Goes Business" in the title of a Finnish comedy, and is called Johnny in a Spaghetti Western version. Marianne Faithfull played the female lead, first played on film by Sarah Bernhardt, in one film about this character, while another film about him was the first in which Christopher Lee and Peter Cushing both appeared, the latter in a role later taken by Robin Williams in an unabridged version that saw Ken Dodd play a jester who does not appear in the original play. For 10 points, Nicol Williamson, Mel Gibson, Kenneth Branagh and Laurence Olivier have all starred on screen as which Shakespearean Prince of Denmark?

Two characters in this novel take the healing elixir called the "balms of Firearbras", which causes them to be sick. In this work, a character is told that a wizard has incinerated his library. The titular "ingenious nobleman" travels on Rosinante and persuades his neighbor Sancho Panza to accompany him on his adventures. Windmills are believed to be giants in, for 10 points, what novel by Miguel de Cervantes that sees a man go mad with chivalry?
acceptableAnswers: The Ingenious Gentleman Don Quixote of La Mancha
El ingenioso hidalgo Don Quixote de la Mancha

tossups.text: This hero accidentally hit Derbforgaill [DEV-or-gill] with a sling and sucked the stone out of her side, then collapsed a house on 150 women after they jealously killed Derbforgaill. Fand, the wife of Manannan mac Lir, nearly stole this man away from his wife Emer before Manannan caused him to forget her. This hero's death came after Lugaid took revenge for the death of his father Cu Roi. This hero was mentored by Scathach, who gave him a spear made of the bones of a sea monster. This man resisted the temptations of the Morrigan while fighting off Queen Medb when she attempted the Cattle Raid of Cooley. For 10 points, name this hero of the Ulster cycle of Irish mythology.

Aelius Gallus laid siege to this city in 25 BCE after being led on a 6-month circuitous march by the traitor Syllaeus, although he was only able to hold it for a week before returning to Alexandria. Denizens of this city used the Musnad script, and Augustus listed this city among his conquests in the Res Gestae. Medieval Arabic writers claimed that this city was home to some of the 7 temples dedicated to the 7 planets that this city's empire worshipped as intermediaries between humans and God, and some Muslim scholars trace the development of Sharia Law to this city, which became rich from trade in frankincense and myrrh. This city's Great Dam, considered to be one of the oldest extant in the world, was constructed in the 2nd millennium BCE to collect water from monsoon rains which feed the Wadi Adhanah in the shadow of the Balaq Hills. According to the Bible, this city served as the capital for the Queen of Sheba, and it remained a prominent city until the fall of the empire it controlled to the Himyarites. For 10 points, what is this capital of the Sabaean Kingdom, and current base of operations for Al Qaeda in Yemen?

A poem written in this language claims that despite an object's release "from the bottom of a shipwreck," "A throw of the dice will never abolish chance." Another poem written in this language wonders, "how comical, how ugly, and how meek / appears" the titular animal, which it later describes as "monarch of the clouds" in comparison to "the Poet." That poem in this language appears is entitled "The Albatross" and appears in a collection with sections like "Revolt," "Wine," and "Spleen and Ideal." For 10 points, name this language used primarily by Stephane Mallarme and Charles Baudelaire, the poet of Les Fleurs du Mal.

In a book about this event, Eliahou is abandoned by his son while on a long march in the snow, and the protagonist and his father are told to say they are eighteen and forty years old after being separated from Tziporah, Hilda, and Bea. Moshe the Beadle's warning about this event is ignored in the first section of a 1960 book by a survivor of this event. For 10 points, name this historical event that provides the backdrop for Elie Wiesel's Night, which describes atrocities committed in the Buchenwald and Auschwitz concentration camps?

The inherited form of this disease has been linked to presenilin 1 and 2 genes, as well as the apoE4 gene on chromosome 19. Hyperphosphorylation of tau proteins figures into the tau hypothesis concerning the pathogenesis of this disease. A better-known hypothesis is the amyloid beta hypothesis, which suggests that the buildup of amyloid beta plaques is responsible. Perhaps the oldest theory concerning this disease is that it is caused by a shortage of acetylcholine in the brain. For 10 points, name this neurodegenerative disease primarily affecting the elderly whose symptoms include memory loss.

Corticosterone, in addition to regulating CRF, is the best-understood regulator of this hormone. The presence of the 1a class of receptors for this hormone in the brain has been linked to social recognition and affiliative behavior, while that of the 1b class is associated with aggression. It achieves its principal function by promoting the release of aquaporins and, like aldosterone, increase in its production is caused by angiotensin II. It is primarily produced in the supraoptic nucleus and, like the structurally similar oxytocin, released from the hypothalamus via the posterior pituitary gland. For 10 points, name this hormone, which constricts blood vessels and restricts water loss in the kidneys.

One thinker from this school of thought used the example of how to pay for a horse-car fare to support the idea that all questions begin with Doubt and Belief. Another thinker from this school compares those who follow "principles," who he calls "tender-minded," with those who follow "facts," who he calls "tough- minded." That thinker from this school used a man chasing a squirrel around a tree to explain this school's namesake method. This school was founded by Charles Sanders Peirce and popularized by William James. For 10 points, name this philosophical school that measures value through its practical application.

Veronique Ovalde was the last winner of a subsidiary award to this prize, for her work in a specific sub-field. This prize was first awarded in 1903; in the same year, a "counter-prize" was set up with an all-female jury in protest of this prize's all-male jury. In 2021, Francois Noudelmann was included on a list of finalists despite his partner, Camille Laurens, being part of this prize's jury. Although this prize is only awarded to an author once, one person won twice under the name Emile Ajar and then their real name Romain Gary. The most recent Nobel laureate to win this award was Patrick Modiano, who won this prize more than 35 years before his Nobel. For 10 points, what prize is considered the highest accolade in French literature?

this structure is essential for heart valves and their functions. It plays a key role in the cardiovascular system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this atrium-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The atrium is a key component of the Cardiovascular system, involved in heart valves and their functions.

tossups.text: Neutron-degenerate matter can become one of these entities above the Tollman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff limit, and quasars are often found around them. These objects have only three externally measurable properties: mass, charge, and angular momentum, according to the "no-hair theorem", and they allegedly evaporate via Hawking radiation. Physics breaks down at their singularities, inside their event horizons. For 10 points, name these incredibly dense stellar remnants from which nothing, not even light, can escape.

In a novel set in this city, the eleven-year-old Anna Kerrigan and her father Eddie befriend a gangster named Dexter. That novel is the most recent novel by Jennifer Egan. Theodore Decker survives a terrorist attack at a museum in this city in the Donna Tartt novel The Goldfinch. City of Glass, Ghosts, and The Locked Room make up a postmodern detective fiction trilogy named for this city by Paul Auster. Newland Archer spots his fiancee May Welland in the box at an opera in this city in the opening scene of The Age of Innocence. Francie Nolan comes of age in this city in a Betty Smith novel named for a tree growing in one of its boroughs. For 10 points name, this large American city, the primary setting of A Tree Grows in Brooklyn.

In Ted Maiman's first functional example of these devices, the gain medium, where population inversion was achieved, was a ruby crystal. These devices use stimulated emission to create a coherent beam of light at a single wavelength, allowing a tighter focus than a traditional lamp. Optical disk drives read data off DVDs by using, for 10 points, what type of device that emits a colored beam of light?

An early leader of an artistic movement that used this form made petroleum-based paints called "Atlcolors" and used the pseudonym Dr. Atl. An artist best known for creating paintings in this form built a namesake Polyforum that houses his painting March of Humanity. A painting in this form originally slated for the lobby of 30 Rock was canceled for its depiction of Vladimir Lenin. David Siqueiros was among the many mid-20th-century Mexican painters who worked in this form. One work in this form is Detroit Industry by Diego Rivera. Leonardo's Last Supper was painted in this form on one side of the dining hall of the Convent of Santa Maria della Grazie. For 10 points, name these large-scale artworks painted on a wall or other permanent surface.
acceptableAnswers: prompt on fresco by asking "what is the larger genre of painting that fresco is a part of?"

tossups.text: One figure by this name betrayed Megara to Minos by pulling a purple hair from the head of King Nisus. Another character with this name fell in love with a fisherman who achieved immortality by chewing on a mysterious plant, Glaucus. When Circe fell for Glaucus as well, this woman's bathwater was poisoned with an agent that caused her to change shape. For 10 points, name this woman with six dogs' heads attached to her, who pestered sailors at the Strait of Messina along with the whirpool Charybdis (kuh-RIB-diss).

Calcium ions are stored in muscle cells by an adapted form of this organelle whose name instead includes the prefix "sarco-". Vesicles coated in COP II["cop two"]travelfromthis organelle to the Golgi apparatus. This organelle, which plays a role in protein folding, may or may not be covered in ribosomes. For ten points, name this organelle that transports proteins through the cell and comes in smooth and rough forms.

parts.text: Name this southernmost Scandinavian country, whose island of Zealand contains its capital of Copenhagen.
Denmark comprises this peninsula and many islands. The southern portion of this peninsula is owned by Germany as part of the state of Schleswig-Holstein (SHLESS-wig HOLE-stine).
This city, Denmark's second largest and the largest on Jutland (JUT-lund), is located next to the Kattegat (KAT-uh-gat). This city is nicknamed "the world's smallest big city."

bonuses.leadin: This country is home to the world's longest continuously-operating amusement park, the Bakken. For 10 points each:

parts.text: This photographer's works include Jewish Giant, taken at Home with His Parents in the Bronx. She also took the photo Child with Toy Hand Grenade in Central Park.
Two children appear in this photograph by Dorothea Lange, which is named for and depicts Florence Thompson.

This 1992 book by Sally Mann was controversial for including several nude shots of her own children. Her son Emmett refused to let one picture appear in the book because it showed him with his socks on his hands.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer the following about children in photographs:

parts.text: Identify this nonmetal element with symbol C and atomic number 6.
Because carbon can form up to four covalent bonds, it makes the backbone of many important biological compounds. This is the name of the study of carbon-containing compounds.
The simplest carbon-based molecules, such as ethane and octane, consist of carbon and this other element.

bonuses.leadin: Diamond and graphite are both allotropes of this element. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify this conversation poem named for an instrument sounded by the wind.
"The Eolian Harp" was written by this poet, whose other works include "Frost at Midnight" and "Christabel," along with one that states "Water, water, every where / Nor any drop to drink."
This poem by Coleridge, the writing of which was interrupted by a "person from Porlock," describes the title figure's "stately pleasure-dome" in Xanadu, where "Alph, the sacred river, ran."

bonuses.leadin: This poem was written two months before its author married Sara Fricker, whose "soft cheek reclined," and the title object of this poem is "placed length-ways in the clasping casement." For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these characters, two of which in the epilogue of a play are dubbed the new Adam and Eve by Alquist.
This science fiction writer wrote about the love between the robots Primus and Helena in RUR . He also wrote the satirical novel War with the Newts .
Capek was from this European country, where the first copies of RUR were published in Prague.

bonuses.leadin: In one play, these characters lead a revolt after Helena Glory burns a manuscript. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this substance which was obtained by a figure after he tricked nine slaves into killing each other by throwing his whetstone into the air.x
While disguised as Bolverk, this Norse god stole the Mead of Poetry. This father of Baldr [ball-dur] and Thor hanged himself from Yggdrasil for nine days and nights to understand the runes.

Besides the Mead of Poetry, Odin also kept one of these objects belonging to Mimir for counsel. Another of these objects belonging to Bran was apparently buried facing towards France in order to ward off invasions.

bonuses.leadin: A portion of this thing that came out of a figure's anus is known as the "rhymester's share" and is thus available to anyone. For 10 points each:

parts.text: The Anapanasati Sutta instructs readers on how to breathe while in the state of sati. Thomas Rhys Davids first translated "sati" as this English term, which psychologists like Jon Kabat-Zinn have since adopted to describe placing one's attention on present-moment experiences.

This co-founder of the Plum Village Monastery translated the Sutta in his Awakening of the Heart. This Vietnamese monk also wrote The Miracle of Mindfulness and founded the socially conscious movement of Engaged Buddhism.
The Anapanasati Sutta is part of the Pali canon, a group of sacred texts used in this branch of Buddhism primarily practiced in Southeast Asia. This branch of Buddhism is contrasted with Mahayana.

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following relating to the Anapanasati Sutta, for 10 points each:

parts.text: meets these two similarly-named characters from a John Byrom nursery rhyme. Although physically twins, they are extremely argumentative contrarians.
evolutionary biologist Leigh Van Valen has named a theory of molecular evolution after this villainous card character, whom finally captures in a game of chess.
This is the name of 's cat, who makes an appearance in Through the Looking Glass with her two kittens.

bonuses.leadin: Name the following characters meets in Through the Looking Glass For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this novel in which Arronax, along with his servant Conseil and the harpooner Ned Land, is kidnapped by the Nautilus and brought to the titular location.
parts.answer: Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea
acceptableAnswers: Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea
The Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea

parts.text: Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea was written by this French author. Phileas Fogg wins a bet due to the International Date Line in this author's Around the World in Eighty Days.
This captain of the Nautilus is nicknamed the "angel of hatred" after ramming and destroying another ship, seemingly to revenge his family.

bonuses.leadin: At the beginning of this novel, Professor Pierre Arronax is brought aboard the Abraham Lincoln in order to investigate a mysterious sea monster. For 10 points-

parts.text: Name this type of reaction, exemplified by one that reacts a diene and dienophile to form a cyclohexene derivative, the Diels-Alder reaction. These reactions involve molecules joining together and forming a ring.
acceptableAnswers: prompt on Diels–Alder reaction before mention

parts.text: The total type of this quantity, up to 1873 for the new Diels-Alderase, is a measure of the number of substrates acted upon by the enzyme throughout its life per active site. This quantity is equal to V-max over catalyst site concentration.
One of the enzymes with the highest turnover number is carbonic anhydrase, which converts bicarbonate ions in the blood into this molecule in the lungs, which we then breathe out.

bonuses.leadin: Recently, the first enzyme that catalyzes a reaction of this type was found in the mulberry tree, and that enzyme is used in the last step of the synthesis of chalcomoracin. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Give the term for these variables, which are altered by the designers of studies or experiments in order to study whether a change results.
In statistical modeling, "dummy" variables, which are used to refer to categories such as race and education level, have this property, like the variables in Boolean algebra.
acceptableAnswers: descriptive answers like “having only two values”

parts.text: Seasonal dummy variables may be used to account for changes during the year when performing analysis on this kind of panel data. A list of daily closing values of a stock exchange is an example of data in this form.

bonuses.leadin: In a model represented as y equals a x plus b, where y represents the outcome, x would be the variable of this type. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify this book that proposes the concept of Dasein to refer to the concept of "being there."
Being and Time was written by this German philosopher, a student of Edmund Husserl.
Heidegger supported this political ideology, as did many other German thinkers at the time. Heidegger's anti-Semitic Black Notebooks are considered to support this ideology.

bonuses.leadin: This work discusses three stages that an individual undergoes: "thrown-ness," existence, and "fallen-ness." For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this 1989 story which follows a car trip taken by the butler Stevens.
This author of When We Were Orphans and An Artist of the Floating World wrote The Remains of the Day.
Expanded from his earlier story "A Strange and Sometimes Sadness," this Ishiguro novel examines the effects of Keiko's suicide on her mother Etsuko and sister Niki.

bonuses.leadin: Mr. Farraday purchases Darlington Hall in this novel. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with parathyroid hormone.
What is the main function of the thyroid in the endocrine system?
Name another component of the endocrine system related to parathyroid hormone.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human endocrine system.

parts.text: Name this traditional scale of mineral hardness. Diamond ranks a 10 on this scale because it can scratch all common materials.
At the opposite end of the Mohs scale from diamond is this very soft mineral, used as a coating on rubber gloves and sometimes found in baby powder.
Hydroxyapatite [hide-rox-ee-ap-ah-tite] ranks halfway between talc and diamond and, in the body, acts as a storage bank for this element.

bonuses.leadin: A sclerometer is normally used to find a mineral's rank on this scale, though the Vickers scale has largely replaced it. For 10 points each,

parts.text: Name this novel about Frederic Moreau, who is in love with the older Madame Arnoux. This novel is semi autobiographical and takes place during the era of the Second French Republic.

Sentimental Education is the last published novel of this French author. He also wrote a historical novel set in Carthage entitled Salammbo and his Three Tales include "A Simple Heart," a short story about the loving servant girl Felicite.

Flaubert is best known for this 1856 novel in which the title character has an affair despite being married to a provincial doctor. This novel was notoriously attacked as being obscene by prosecutors.

bonuses.leadin: One character in this novel is the math teacher Senecal, who ultimately becomes a policeman. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these closed loops through which electric current can flow. These paths may be arranged in series or in parallel.

For a parallel circuit, the equivalent amount of this quantity is found by summing the reciprocal of each component's value and then taking the reciprocal of the total. This quantity is equal to voltage divided by current according to Ohm's law.
This generalized form of resistance is applied to alternating current circuits where it is expressed as a complex number, combining resistance with reactance.

bonuses.leadin: The symbol for an inductor resembles a coiled wire on the diagrams for these entities. For 10 points each,

parts.text: Name this "Painter of Light" whose landscapes were championed by John Ruskin. He lends his name to the U.K's foremost contemporary art prize, which has controversially been awarded to Tracey Emin and Damien Hirst.

A Turner painting depicts The Fighting Temeraire about to be "broken up" after this battle. Edwin Landseer sculpted 4 lions surrounding a monument in the center of a square named for this battle in London.

In his will, Turner gifted the National Gallery two paintings on the condition they were hung next to two landscapes by this French Baroque artist. This man's Embarkation of the Queen of Sheba inspired Turner's Dido Building Carthage.

bonuses.leadin: In response to an1846 whaling scene by this artist, the Almanack of the Month made a caricature of him using a mop and bucket to paint. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Alviss was killed by this Norse god. He once lost a wrestling match to a personification of Old Age, and he will kill his archenemy, the World Serpent, at Ragnarok before walking nine paces and dying.

Thor was unhappy about his daughter Thrud being promised to Alviss, so he asked Alviss questions to test his wisdom until the sun came up, which did this to the dwarf. The gaze of Medusa also performed this action.
Being a dwarf, Alviss' homeworld would have been this dark world in Norse mythology.

bonuses.leadin: Alviss the dwarf was very abused during his lifetime. Answer some questions about him for 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this fourth state of matter created by heating a gas or applying an electromagnetic field.
Plasmas typically act as these substances that allow electrons to flow freely through them.
In plasma physics, this device is used to contain plasmas for study. Its name derives from a Russian acronym meaning "toroidal chamber with magnetic coils."

bonuses.leadin: When enough energy is put into a gas, it can become ionized to this substance. For 10 points each:
